name: ignorance
description: The state of not knowing or having incorrect knowledge about something. The sensations involved depend on whether you're aware of not knowing and how other people perceive actions based on that lack of knowledge.

variations.name: known ignorance
variations.description: The awareness that you lack an area of knowledge along with humility enough to be careful avoid acting as if you had that knowledge.
perceptions: I know that I don't know this topic.
I'm not going to pretend I do.
I will defer to others who have more knowledge on this topic.
examples: advising someone to see a doctor
not weighing in on a topic you're not familiar with

guidance.description: Making decisions with incomplete information is a common challenge in many situations, such as business, personal, or social. How can you avoid making mistakes or missing opportunities when you don't have all the facts? Here are some tips to help you make better decisions with incomplete information.

variations.name: innocent ignorance
variations.description: The sense that someone else doesn't properly understand a certain topic, but you as an external observer don't expect them to know that thing.
perceptions: A sense that someone else just revealed that there's something they don't understand.
A recognition that it's ok for them to not have known.
results: trying to decide whether to correct the other person's misunderstanding
examples: someone asked about your relative who recently passed away
a young child asks an embarrassing question

guidance.description: When someone doesn't know something that they can't be expected to know, you should consider gently correcting them.

variations.name: self-centered ignorance
variations.description: The sense that someone else doesn't properly understand a certain topic, but you as an external observer feel that they should know better.
perceptions: A sense that someone else just revealed that there's something they don't understand.
A judgment that they should have known this thing.
results: trying to decide how to respond to the knowledge gap
examples: not knowing that texting while driving is unsafe

guidance.description: It may be helpful to understand the 'Dunning-Kruger Effect'. This is a bias that can cause beginners to be over-confident and experts to be under-confident.
This kind of ignorance can come with (or be caused by) overconfidence. There are online tips for dealing with people you view as overconfident.

variations.name: willful ignorance
variations.description: The awareness that you lack an area of knowledge along with a sense that the area is unimportant or even dangerous, and it's fair to disrespect others' knowledge of this area.
perceptions: I know that I don't know this topic well.
I do not want to understand this topic because it's uncomfortable, dangerous, or could be damaging to me socially.
People who claim knowledge of this area are safe to ignore.
examples: distrust for people who have knowledge of 'inappropriate' topics

guidance.description: You should be aware that other people might not perceive your willful ignorance as a positive. They may find it disrespectful or even contemptuous.

comparisons.description: 'Willful ignorance' invokes social tension in people who have knowledge of an area. It's fine to avoid knowledge areas that you find inappropriate or disturbing. That could count as 'known ignorance' as long as you don't act as if you understand it. For example, you might not like horror movies, so avoid exposing yourself to them. It is 'willful ignorance' if you make a statement like 'Everyone who enjoys horror movies is a twisted psycho,' since that reveals a broad-brush stereotype to those people. A statement like 'Horror movies are not for me' will be perceived as ok. If you really wanted to be an activist to convince people to stop watching horror movies, you would have to research the effects and therefore lose the ignorance.

variations.name: realized ignorance
variations.description: An after-the-fact realization that you had acted out of ignorance or false knowledge. The reaction will depend on the consequences and your personality.
perceptions: I had been acting on false information or had failed to learn before acting.
results: decide to admit ignorance with humility
deny the importance of the event

guidance.description: It can be difficult grappling with the limitations of one tiny human brain against an infinitely complicated world. You have to move forward amidst social pressures and instincts. Good luck.

variations.name: self ignorance
variations.description: Things are happening inside that you don't understand.
perceptions: I don't know why I'm reacting this way.
results: decide to admit ignorance with humility
deny the importance of the event

commentaries.quote: There's an infinite amount that can be known, so we're all ignorant of a lot. What matters is how we handle acting on doubt and the inevitable revelation of a blank spot.
Some of us are so terrified of drowning in ignorance that we become obsessive lifelong learners who watch documentaries for fun. Others swim happily in their ignorance. People.
The greatest obstacle to discovery is not ignorance - it is the illusion of knowledge.
If you think education is expensive, try ignorance.
Facts do not cease to exist because they are ignored.

There is a cult of ignorance in the United States, and there has always been. The strain of anti-intellectualism has been a constant thread winding its way through our political and cultural life, nurtured by the false notion that democracy means that 'my ignorance is just as good as your knowledge.

Ignorance is indeed a marvelous power if a human learned how to use it, it can create worlds and situations and strengthen the energy of the mind giving such control on the way you receive and send human senses and reactions, it happens in so many levels that a regular person can't feel or notice it. Ignorance is not always bad after all!
